<strong>Antes de buscar el equilibrio, t: Before looking for the equilibrium, cross out the dominated strategies. A three-by-three matrix usually comes down to two-by-two and the equilibrium appears in plain sight.
<strong>Dibuja el grafo aunque te lo den: Draw the graph even if you are given a table. Degrees, cycles and connectedness are seen in the drawing and miscounted in the list of edges.
<strong>La complejidad se pregunta en el: Complexity is asked about in the worst case. An algorithm that is almost always fast may be quadratic, and what gets marked is the bound, not the impression.
<strong>La entropía se mide en bits y es: Entropy is measured in bits and it is an average. It comes from adding $p\log_2(1/p)$, and comparing it with the average length of the code is what says whether the code is good.
Cada tramo aporta un número fijo de preg: Each section contributes a fixed number of questions, drawn at random from its topics without repeating a topic while that is possible, and avoiding the most basic exercises. With 6 topics and 6 questions, one exam covers almost the whole block: that is why the link at the end reproduces the same exam, and “another exam” draws a different one.
Cómo sacarle partido: How to get the most out of it
El enlace de un examen corregido reprodu: The link to a marked exam reproduces the same questions with the same numbers. A teacher can do one, copy the link and pass it to the class: everyone will sit the same exam and will be able to compare results and procedures.
El problema de los siete puentes de Köni: The problem of the seven bridges of Königsberg was, in 1736, an after-dinner puzzle: can you cross them all exactly once? Euler answered no, and to answer it he threw the map away and kept only what was joined to what. That gesture —keeping the structure and throwing away the geometry— founded graph theory, and it is exactly what the questions in the first section ask for.
Elige los tramos que entran. Las pregunt: Choose the sections to include. The questions are drawn at random from the exercises of each topic in the block, avoiding the most basic ones and without repeating a topic while possible. There are no hints: the marking and the step-by-step solution come on submitting.
Error de un método numérico y cuántas it: The error of a numerical method and how many iterations are needed; the entropy of a source and the average length of a code; the payoff matrix, the dominant strategy and the Nash equilibrium.
Eso no se sabe de ningún problema de NP:: That is not known of any problem in NP: it is the P versus NP problem. Besides, every problem in P is also in NP.
Examen de matemática discreta y computac: Exam on discrete and computational mathematics
Grados y caminos en un grafo; árbol de r: Degrees and paths in a graph; the minimum spanning tree and the shortest path; solving a linear recurrence; ordering algorithms by their complexity and deciding whether a problem is in P or in NP.
Los más difíciles de NP son los NP-compl: The hardest ones in NP are the NP-complete ones, which are a part of it. Adding two numbers is also in NP and it is not hard.
NP es la clase de los problemas cuya res: NP is the class of problems whose answer, if you are given it, is quickly verified. Finding it may be extremely slow, and whether it is fast or not is precisely the open question.
Que es uno de los problemas más difícile: That it is one of the hardest problems there is
Que no se puede resolver en tiempo polin: That it cannot be solved in polynomial time
Que una solución propuesta se puede comp: That a proposed solution can be checked in polynomial time
Seis temas sobre lo que se cuenta y sobr: Six topics about what gets counted and about what a computer computes: networks, recurrences, algorithms, information and decisions. This topic teaches nothing new: it asks. A procedural exam with exercises from the whole block, with a clock and no hints.
Un examen de bloque es un simulacro hech: A block exam is a mock paper taken at home: with a clock, no notes and no hints. The questions come from the exercises of the 6 topics of the block, spread across sections, and every time you start one the numbers are different and so are the topics: doing it several times covers the whole block. On submission everything is marked, the step-by-step solution of each question opens, and the mark comes out section by section, with links to what is worth revising. The “tailored to what you have done” option puts first what you have not solved yet: it is the way to check that no topic is left untouched.
Un problema está en NP. ¿Qué significa e: A problem is in NP. What does that mean exactly?
